in.role: Led Carolina in every receiving category

doFirst.why: Coker went 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores — 29.8 points — and led the Panthers in every receiving category while McMillan was quiet until garbage time. He is 50% rostered, which in a ten-team league is an anomaly rather than a verdict. Carolina draw Atlanta then Cleveland next. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim costs nothing lasting, and Stafford is a second quarterback behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league — the least valuable thing on the roster.

candidates.note: Ownership moved +3.40, the largest on the board — and the move is already wrong. Schefter reports the Raiders believe Bowers misses only week 1 and returns at the Chargers. The market is pricing week 1's box score; the news has moved on. Do not chase this.

Same story as Mayer. The Bowers target vacuum that made him interesting probably closes this week. His 94.9% snap share is still real and makes him worth watching if Bowers' knee lingers, but the reason to add him has a return date on it.

56 attempts, 410 yards, three touchdowns, and New Orleans are 7.5-point underdogs to Baltimore next. A volume quarterback on a team that will trail all season. Only relevant here as an Allen bye-week patch in week 7 — and Chem priority resets, so that claim will be free when you need it.

A.J. Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks with a high ankle sprain. Doubs, not Mack Hollins, is the receiver to have — Hollins played more but was blocking in a run-heavy plan. Rostered by a Chem rival, so this is trade leverage as much as a wire note.
